questions: With kp 3.5 at wheel_track 0.09 m, does oval steering_oscillation fall below 0.25 while progress stays near 0.73?
Does the score stay at or above 153.01? If it falls, is the controller change the cause, given that the geometry is held?
Do slalom line_loss_events fall back from 2 toward 1, or does the lower kp make line loss worse?
Does s-bend max_error stay near 0.063 m, which would show that track width alone cannot reach the 0.06 m floor?
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If oval steering_oscillation is still above 0.25 at kp 3.5, report the kp you need so I can judge whether geometry is the limit. If the score is above 153 and s-bend max_error is still above 0.06 m with oscillation below 0.25, I may consider wheel_track 0.08 m in a later iteration, but only with kp lowered to match. If the score falls below 153, tell me the controller settings so I can separate controller from geometry effects.

intent: Hold the iteration 6 geometry exactly (wheel_track 0.09 m, five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m and y = 0.04 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.18 m, mass 0.6 kg) so the race isolates the Integrator's controller change (kp 3.5). Expected result: a score at or above 153, oval steering_oscillation below about 0.25, and oval and s-bend line_loss_events near 1 per run. No geometry change this iteration.
learning: Iteration 6 suggests the platform is gaining from narrower tracks mainly through oval progress, not s-bend tracking. Track-width gains are likely to flatten because the s-bend max_error did not move from 0.0626 to 0.063 m. Holding geometry while testing kp will show whether the remaining limit is yaw gain (oscillation) or sensing or inertia.
rationale: Iteration 6 (wheel_track 0.09 m, five 12 mm sensors at y = 0.04 m, mass 0.6 kg) is the best result so far at 153.01, up from 112.54. The gain is mostly on the oval, where progress rose from 0.55 to 0.73 and 2 of 20 trials finished. The narrowing from 0.10 to 0.09 m therefore worked as a yaw-authority change on the oval. The evidence has also stopped pointing at geometry. S-bend max_error did not improve (0.0626 m at 0.10 m, 0.063 m at 0.09 m), so the 0.06 m floor is not being approached by track width alone. Slalom line loss rose from 1 to 2 events per run, and oval steering_oscillation is 0.2505, just above the 0.25 caution level. Further narrowing to 0.08 m would raise yaw gain again by about 12 percent. That would likely worsen oscillation and slalom line loss without a demonstrated benefit on the s-bend, so I do not propose it. Sensing changes (seven sensors, 16 mm footprints, y = 0.03 m) all lowered the score in earlier iterations, so I keep the five-sensor layout. The Integrator's controller change (kp 3.5 at 0.09 m) is the variable to test this iteration. Changing geometry at the same time would confound it, so I hold every geometry value at iteration 6's settings. The only geometry change I considered, a body or mass change to cut yaw inertia, is not supported by evidence, since mass was confounded with track width in iteration 2 and the contract's body_length wording is inconsistent on whether it affects dynamics. I expect the held geometry with kp 3.5 to keep the oval oscillation below 0.25 and to keep or improve the 153 score. If the score falls below 153, the controller change, not the geometry, is the likely cause.
